name: openfoam
summary: Computational fluid dynamics platform for flow, heat transfer, and multiphysics engineering analysis.
why_it_matters: OpenFOAM remains important engineering capability knowledge, but current Vrooli usage does not justify maintaining the solver stack as an active supported resource.
when_to_use: A future scenario needs CFD or heat-transfer analysis.
Operators want local or containerized engineering simulation workflows.
The workflow depends on solver-driven analysis rather than a lightweight calculator.

platform_support.notes: Containerization is possible, but HPC assumptions, solver performance, and toolchain complexity still make support uneven across hosts.

prerequisites: Validated solver image or host install path
Reference case files and sample benchmarks
Artifact storage for inputs, meshes, and results
implementation_notes: Promotion should validate a specific case-running workflow.
Keep preprocessing, solve execution, and postprocessing as separate concerns.
Do not claim support without tested reference cases.
operational_notes: Performance and artifact size matter as much as installation.
Validation should include a real sample case solve.
Long-running jobs need timeout and cleanup policies.
risks: Scientific solver wrappers become maintenance debt without active users.
Unsupported host assumptions can fail in opaque ways.
